quotes.verbatim_quote:
The Program is made up of a series of project lessons, each lasting

50 minutes per day, running six consecutive days per week, with

one day off.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the foundational daily and weekly practice regimen that the entire 20-week program rests on.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
The objective is to gradually increase the tempo over

the course of 20 weeks to reach a metronome setting of approximately
= 126 (maintaining precision and accuracy at all times).
quotes.why_load_bearing: States the program's measurable endpoint and the critical qualifier that speed must never come at the expense of precision.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
The First Six Weeks, Project Lessons 1-A, 1-B, 2-A, 2-B, 3-A, 3-B,
focus on the use of eighth notes, as representative of duple time,
sixteenth notes, thirty-second notes, etc.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Identifies the rhythmic scope of the first phase, anchoring duple subdivisions to eighth notes as the primary vehicle.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Project Lesson 1-B uses the same chord progression transposed to
another key, thus requiring a change of fingering patterns, licks,

etc. This also tends to stimulate fresh approaches and ideas.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Explains the pedagogical rationale for key transposition: it forces new fingering solutions and creative thinking, not merely mechanical repetition.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Weeks Eight Through Thirteen, Project Lessons 4-A, 4-B, 5-A, 5-B,

6-A, 6-B focus on triple time via eighth note triplets as representative

of their relative divisions and sub-divisions, i.e., quarter note triplets,
sixteenth note triplets, etc.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Marks the pivot from duple to triple time, establishing triplet feel as the organizing principle for the program's second phase.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Review the projecat lessons in any order to establish your present
maximum tempo as a permanent reflex.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Introduces the concept of tempo as a motor reflex rather than a conscious effort, which is the target neurological outcome of the review weeks.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Review the project lessons as before using (a) hammer-on's
(b)pull-off's (c) glissandi (slides). The introduction of these
techniques should cause your technique 'and speed to increase
dramatically in that via these devices several notes can be pro-
duced with one picking stroke.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Prescribes the specific legato devices for the final phase and explains the mechanical reason they accelerate speed: multiple notes per pick stroke.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
The Appendix in the back of the book consists of examples or
models of the kind of lines intended for the project lessons and
are numbered accordingly, i.e. 1-A, 1-B, 2-A, 2-B, etc.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Directs the student to the reference material that supplies the actual musical content for each project lesson, without which the program structure cannot be applied.
